decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach to the coin; bank is in right workspace, so plan a central handoff.
Continue smooth elbow-up sweep, orienting the left fingers down toward the holder.
Approach above the left holder while completing downward gripper alignment; maintain open jaws.
Finish the downward approach, then use wrist imagery for millimetric centering before closing.
Wrist view places the coin above the pinch point; shift the left wrist along its approach plane and lower slightly while partially closing.
Center the coin edge between the left jaws and correct its small angular mismatch before the final pinch.
Correct the wrist-view overshoot with small in-plane translations, keeping the coin between partially open jaws.
Complete the centered pinch and perform a short vertical retention test; judge the coin from images.
Lift the pinched coin clear of the holder by more than eight centimeters, retaining the closed left gripper.
The coin stayed in the holder during the lift. Reopen and return with a deeper in-plane overlap for a secure pinch.
Align the coin with the jaw center and increase overlap before fully closing; previous pinch missed the coin.
Close fully around the overlapping coin edge and raise only two centimeters to check actual retention.
Continue a vertical retention test with the left gripper closed; the coin is partly occluded by the fingers.
Retention failed again. Return with open fingers and a lower grasp height, then inspect before closing.
At the lower height the coin projects too far behind the pinch point. Shift forward in-plane to center it while bringing the jaws close.
Use small diagonal corrections to bring the coin face back onto the jaw center at the lower grasp height.
The coin now overlaps the pinch region at the lower height. Close completely, settle, then test a small lift.
Raise vertically with closed jaws and compare the coin against the holder to verify retention.
The holder still contains the coin. Lower the open gripper further so the pads engage the coin faces rather than only its rim.
Coin is centered at the deeper approach height. Close and settle without lifting to inspect pad contact.
Test the deeper pinch with a slow two-centimeter vertical lift and watch whether the coin separates from its holder.
Continue the retention check slowly; the coin remains near the finger tips but separation from the holder is not yet clear.
The gold edge now appears retained while the holder recedes. Lift farther clear with closed jaws before preparing a handoff.
Coin is visibly clear of the holder. Begin a gradual left-wrist rotation toward the central handoff, keeping the grasp closed and elbow-up.
Rotate the held coin gradually toward the center while starting the right arm's open receiving approach in its own workspace.
Continue coordinated approach toward a central handoff, retaining the visible coin and keeping both elbow-up configurations continuous.
Bring both wrists closer to the handoff while rotating the left grasp toward a horizontal presentation; right jaws stay open.
Continue to the central transfer pose with the left coin retained; slow the right receiving wrist as it nears its final orientation.
Bring the receiving wrist to face the center and continue rotating the retained coin into the handoff plane, without crossing arms.
Finish presenting the coin horizontally at the center; keep the receiving fingers open for visual alignment.
Align the right receiving pinch to the visible coin with small lateral and height corrections; the left gripper keeps holding.
Center the coin in the receiving jaws and close the right gripper while maintaining the left grasp for a supported transfer.
Release the left donor gradually while holding the right receiving pinch fixed; verify the coin stays with the right fingers.
Coin appears retained by the right gripper. Separate the arms, retract the left, and begin turning the right coin downward toward the bank.
No motion executed after the continuity rejection. Retry the right wrist turn with much smaller increments while separating the donor arm.
Continue a small-step right wrist turn with the coin visibly retained, while retracting the open left arm toward home.
Carry the retained coin toward the bank with a gentle wrist rotation; continue returning the empty left arm without crossing workspaces.
Continue the bank approach with a modestly faster wrist turn now clear of the handoff; retract the empty arm smoothly.
Continue the right-arm overhead bank approach with the coin secure; slow the empty left arm near its home pose.
Complete the empty arm's return and continue turning the coin downward above the bank, preserving clearance.
Continue positioning the right wrist over the slot with the coin upright in its grasp; make only tiny home corrections to the left arm.
Complete the downward coin orientation above the bank and use the next wrist view to align the slot before descending.
The slot is slightly to the right of the coin in the wrist image. Translate laterally and refine yaw while remaining above the bank.
Align along the slot and descend slowly; the slot is now just left and forward of the coin in the wrist view.
Correct the remaining lateral offset by a few millimeters and lower the coin into the slot with the gripper still closed.
Make a final millimetric along-slot correction and seat the coin slightly deeper while maintaining its alignment.
Release the aligned coin into the slot while keeping the wrist stationary; inspect before withdrawing.
The coin has left the gripper into the slot. Withdraw vertically with open fingers before returning the right arm home.
The slot is clear of the released coin at the surface. Begin the open right arm's smooth return toward origin, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Continue retracting the empty right gripper toward its starting pose, keeping a smooth elbow-up path clear of the bank.
Return the empty right arm along a smooth, continuous path toward its origin; both grippers remain open.
Continue the empty right arm's return, reducing its height and wrist rotation smoothly toward the initial pose.
Slow the final return near the starting configuration, with open fingers and no further bank contact.
